after: ## Demographic change as cause and effect (4.3.1)
alt: Four chains from cause to effect: contraception, lower infant mortality and the cost of children lead to falling birth rates and smaller families; better diet and medicine raise life expectancy and create beanpole families; both produce an ageing population with more care for parents; delayed parenthood produces older parents and a middle generation caring both ways.
caption: Write each demographic change as a chain: cause, change, effect on family life.

alt: Young and Willmott’s three stages: the pre-industrial family as a unit of production, an early industrial stage of extended kin networks, and a later home-centred symmetrical family. Parsons’s functional fit theory is set against historians who found nuclear households before industrialisation. Urbanisation today often produces modified extended families.
caption: The link between industry and the nuclear family is debated, not settled.

after: ## Why are marriage, divorce and cohabitation changing? (4.3.3)
alt: Six factors around the trends in marriage, divorce and cohabitation, each with its mechanism: legislation, changing attitudes, the internet, secularisation, cultural expectations and female empowerment.
caption: Each factor needs a mechanism, not just a label.

after: ## Why are marriage, divorce and cohabitation changing? (4.3.3)
alt: Four perspectives on rising divorce: functionalists, through Fletcher, see high expectations of marriage and remarriage; the New Right see family breakdown harming children; feminists see women’s independence; late modern writers see the pure relationship (Giddens) and individualisation (Beck and Beck-Gernsheim).
caption: The same trend means decline to some and progress to others.

alt: Conjugal roles are moving towards the symmetrical and dual worker family, though feminists say women keep the main responsibility. Children have become an economic cost, families more child-centred, and boomerang children return home. Grandparents give childcare, economic support and advice, but may later become dependent.
caption: Longer lives and longer childhoods have changed what each generation does.

alt: Two reasons laid out as point, mechanism and link: easier divorce laws let unhappy couples end marriages legally, reducing empty shell marriages; female empowerment means women can leave because they are financially independent, which feminists see as progress.
caption: Change, mechanism, effect: the chain every explain answer needs.
